headline: Week eleven: vert ramps clear of target, calf silent
narrative: The ask was to ramp the vert, and it ramped — the week finished comfortably clear of its target, with time on feet just over the ask as well. Friday's dawn raid on Kinder, repping Grindslow Knoll and Kinder Low, was the centrepiece and did most of the climbing in one big mountain day. The 'longer back-to-back' came out reshaped: instead of a weekend double, the big Friday rolled into Saturday's parkrun and a Sunday indoor vert grind on a steep treadmill and the stairmaster — three consecutive days on feet, with tired-leg climbing on the third. Close in spirit, though a true consecutive-mountain-days weekend is still worth banking before the biggest weeks arrive.

Fourth straight week without a word from the calf, through the heaviest climbing load of the build so far. Cumulatively the push toward Costa Blanca stays on schedule, with three Build weeks now stacked cleanly and each one bigger than the last. Next week is a deload, and the target drops hard — the job is to come in under it, not over. After three ascending weeks, absorbing the work is the training.
